summary: We created a game called Hardware Hunters 4052, where the player is a hardware hunter who is tasked to record hardware left in Earth, Mars and in space from the 1960s to 2026. The problem is that Earth is much weaker now and a lot of asteroids are heading towards it. The good news is that a newly discovered lifeform the Numans are willing to help the player (with their singing powers that can destroy the asteroids) but the player needs to help with the beat. It addresses the challenge because the game covers the hardware in space, along with their specific missions and purpose in an engaging way...through rhythm!!! It's designed to be played casually by players or a younger audience who may not know a lot about the work NASA does. The game includes pictures, 3d models, descriptions of what the hardware does, where it is, and a connection to our fictional story. Things in the game has labels so that the player knows what's real and what's made up, so it's not confusing. This game is important because it educates a younger audience and makes them more aware about NASA and the world around us.
details:
What does it do/How does it work

Every time the player clears a rhythm game by clicking an environment (Earth, Moon or the deep space), they are able to record the hardware in their Hardwaredex (a notebook) and learn more about it. There are multiple interactive features like playing around with the 3D models or looking at photographs. Each rhythm game also has difficulty levels, and there is a way to adjust the keys.

Benefits

The game is educational and fun to play. The player gets immersed in learning about the hardware located throughout space and its importance while also completing games, so it doesn't feel like forced engagement.

Impact

The intended impact of this project is so that more people can learn about the scientific advancements NASA has made throughout the 1960s to present day, and about the importance of each advancement. This makes science accessible to more people.

Tools

  • Claude
  • Vite
  • Three.js
  • HTML, CSS, JavaScript
  • NASA data
  • NeoWS
  • VSCode

Creativity

Our project is creative because it combines music (the arts) with STEM education in an engaging and immersive way.

Considerations

  • We had to consider whether we were going to use non-copyrighted songs or create original ones. We ended up creating original songs because there could be ambiguous implications when using non-copyrighted songs for a project like this.
  • We had to consider how to make our game more appealing in terms of color and accessibility. We made numerous design decisions with colors to make certain buttons pop or highlight where the different hardware was located. We do note that there are more accessibility issues to consider, so we tried our best to address the ones that came to mind the most for this limited time frame.
  • We had to consider what we can actually get done within this limited time frame to make our goals and tasks more realistic.
